name: Clairo
label: Clairo Records
lede: She made a video on a laptop in thirty minutes on the day she thought she looked her worst, and eight years later she was a Coachella headliner with a tape-recorded soul album to her name.

eras.title: A bedroom and a Bandcamp
eras.text: Claire Cottrill grew up in Carlisle, Massachusetts, taught herself guitar partly from YouTube tutorials, and spent her teens posting EPs under two names. A cheap keyboard, a laptop camera and one bad-skin day turned that into a career.

years.h: Five EPs on Bandcamp, two stage names
years.p: Before she was Clairo to most people, Cottrill was uploading Aquarius Boy, Late Show, Moth Girl, Metal Heart and Have a Nice Day, some of it as DJ Baby Benz.

years.cap: Clairo at the Fonda Theatre, 2024 · Wikimedia
q: I didn't intend for it to be a lo-fi song.
years.src: Wikipedia: Pretty Girl · The Fader: Clairo on Pretty Girl
years.h: "Pretty Girl": thirty minutes, a laptop, a Gizmo doll
years.p: Cottrill filmed herself lip-syncing in her childhood bedroom, acne showing, Dunkin' iced coffee in frame. The video went viral on YouTube that August.
years.xp:
She made the song in GarageBand on a MacBook with a small keyboard and '80s pop she'd absorbed from her mother's music, and has said she used "the resources around me which were pretty shitty". The video was filmed in Photo Booth on a day she deliberately felt at her worst. Per Wikipedia it passed 75 million views by 2021.

The song was first recorded for a cassette compilation, The Le Sigh Vol. III, then re-recorded for her debut EP. Its predecessor, "Flaming Hot Cheetos", had come out in June 2017.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pretty Girl · The Ringer: The Curious Case · The Fader: Clairo on Pretty Girl · NME: Clairo interview
years.h: Fader Label signs a college freshman to a 12-song deal
years.p: Wikipedia says the deal came through her father's connection to Jon Cohen, who ran the label's Rubber Tracks studio; The Ringer says she also signed with Chance the Rapper's manager.
years.xp:
By the time The Fader interviewed her in October 2017, Cottrill was 19, just starting at Syracuse University, and already on the label. Major labels including Capitol, Columbia and RCA were reported to be interested, per Wikipedia's Diary 001 article.

She left Syracuse's music business program after one year to go full time, telling NME she didn't want to have to rely on anyone else.

eras.title: Twelve songs and a plant rumor
eras.text: The debut EP arrived with a national tour slot, a sold-out New York room and an internet argument about whether a viral bedroom star had been engineered.

years.h: Diary 001 EP, on Fader Label
years.p: Pitchfork gave her debut EP 7.0; Sasha Geffen wrote that she had worked hard to make it sound this easy. It later went Gold in the US.

years.h: Opening for Dua Lipa, selling out the Bowery Ballroom
years.p: Cottrill supported Dua Lipa's tour, headlined her own Lazy Days dates, sold out New York's Bowery Ballroom in July and played Lollapalooza in August.

q: No, I just have representation, like every single other artist you listen to.
years.src: The Ringer: The Curious Case · Wikipedia: Diary 001
years.h: The "industry plant" argument
years.p: Reddit threads noted that her father Geoff Cottrill had been a marketing executive at Converse, and asked why she hadn't said so. Her answer to the New York Times is on the record.
years.xp:
The Ringer's July 2018 piece laid out the case: Geoff Cottrill was chief marketing officer at Converse and was tied to its Rubber Tracks studio program. The author argued that crediting advertising executives with engineering virality gives them too much credit.

Cottrill called the suspicion a sexist assumption about how women succeed, per Wikipedia's Diary 001 article.

eras.title: Immunity, and a band of friends
eras.text: The debut album moved the sound from lo-fi bedroom to polished soft rock with Rostam Batmanglij in the room. Then the pandemic sent her home to Atlanta and into a band.

years.h: "Bags" becomes the year's breakout single
years.p: Clairo told NME the song came from her first romantic experiences with a girl. BBC Radio 1 ranked it No. 5 on its 2019 Hottest Records list.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, Pitchfork placed "Bags" at No. 3 on its year-end songs list, with The Guardian at No. 9 and Billboard at No. 48. It was nominated for Song of the Year at the Boston Music Awards.

The song was nominated for Best Song in the World at the 2020 NME Awards, where she won Best New Act in the World.

q: I didn't want to have to rely on anyone else.
years.h: Immunity: Rostam in the booth, Danielle Haim on drums
years.p: Clairo produced six tracks herself; Rostam Batmanglij of Vampire Weekend co-produced and co-wrote. Pitchfork gave the album 8.0.
years.xp:
"Sofia" became her first song on the Billboard Hot 100. The album peaked at No. 51 on the Billboard 200 and went Gold in the US, per Wikipedia.

"I Wouldn't Ask You", the nearly seven-minute closer, was inspired by her juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, she told NME. The album was made in Los Angeles and Atlanta.

years.h: Shelly: a band with Claud and two Syracuse friends
years.p: Back in Atlanta during lockdown, Cottrill formed Shelly with [[Claud|34f3e890-c917-4ee1-b859-b22c48e2a42c]], Josh Mehling and Noa Frances Getzug and put out "Steeeam" and "Natural".
years.xp: The band then went quiet. Its next release, the double single "Cross Your Mind" and "Hartwell", came in July 2025, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Sling, the quiet one
eras.text: Clairo traded synths for piano, strings and folk-rock with Jack Antonoff at Allaire and Electric Lady, and then took it on the road with mixed luck.

years.h: "Blouse": Lorde sings backup from New Zealand
years.p: Antonoff co-produced the first Sling single; Lorde's backing vocals were recorded on a rainy day in New Zealand, and you can hear raindrops.
years.xp: Clairo has said the song is about being sexualized in the music industry. She later played it on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Sling on Republic and Fader Label
years.p: Recorded in 2020 at Allaire Studios and Electric Lady, it earned an 84 on Metacritic and debuted at No. 17 on the Billboard 200, her first top 20.

years.h: Sling tour: an ear injury in Toronto, a cancelled Bristol night
years.p: Per Wikipedia, an in-ear monitor incident in Toronto caused temporary hearing damage, and a sinusitis-related panic attack cancelled the Bristol show before she finished the UK run in London.
years.xp: At Glastonbury that summer she wore a "Bans Off Our Bodies" T-shirt on stage, protesting restrictions on abortion. In May 2022 she had also signed a full-page New York Times ad with 160 artists responding to the overturning of Roe v. Wade.

eras.title: Charm: soul on tape
eras.text: Clairo left the synths and studio polish behind, cut an album live to analog tape with Leon Michels, and got her first top 10 and first Grammy nomination.

years.cap: Clairo and Leon Michels, Charm sessions.
years.src: BrooklynVegan: Clairo announces · The Line of Best Fit: Clairo Charm · Wikipedia: Charm
years.h: "Sexy to Someone" announces Charm and Leon Michels
years.p: The lead single came with news that Michels, the El Michels Affair leader who has worked with the Dap-Kings, co-produced a fully analog record cut live to tape at Diamond Mine Recording in Queens and Allaire in Woodstock.
years.xp:
BrooklynVegan reported horns, woodwinds and vintage synths on the record. The Line of Best Fit, which gave Charm 8/10, heard Blossom Dearie and Carole King's piano in it.

Allaire is the same woodland studio where she made Sling. The "Sexy to Someone" video, with a yeti, came in December 2024, per Wikipedia and Rolling Stone.

years.h: Charm: Pitchfork gave it 7.5 and ranked it No. 21 of 2024
years.p: Per Wikipedia's reception box, Metacritic scored it 82 and Pitchfork 7.5; Pitchfork later placed it 21st on its 50 best albums of 2024. It became her first US top 10, at No. 8.
years.xp:
The Guardian and NME each gave it five stars, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork's review score was taken from Wikipedia because pitchfork.com could not be fetched.

Singles: "Nomad" (June 28), "Juna" (July 12), "Add Up My Love" (November 1, 2024) and "Terrapin" (February 6, 2025).

years.h: "Juna" on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon
years.p: Five days after the album came out, Clairo played the song live on late-night TV.
years.xp: The Guardian called the performance intimate and light-hearted, and Clash called it a gossamer spider's web of soulful pop, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Still from the "Juna" video, directed by Bradley J. Calder.
years.src: Stereogum: Clairo Juna video · Wikipedia: Juna
years.h: "Juna" video: a VFW-hall wrestling show in Worcester
years.p: Clairo's first professional music video in over six years watches a battle royal, then joins the crowd and poses backstage with the wrestlers.
years.xp:
Bradley J. Calder shot it at Beyond Wrestling's Wrestling Open in Worcester, Massachusetts, per Stereogum. Stereogum noted that none of her first three albums had produced an official video for an album track.

The song reached No. 1 on Billboard's TikTok chart and went Gold in the US, Australia and New Zealand, per Wikipedia.

years.h: First Grammy nomination, and a fall tour with Alice Phoebe Lou
years.p: Charm was nominated for Best Alternative Music Album at the 67th Grammys. The Charm tour ran September to November, with New York and Los Angeles residencies at Webster Hall and the Fonda.

eras.title: Coachella and a new label
eras.text: Charm kept working after its year, and Clairo became a festival main-stage act who talks about politics onstage.

years.h: Coachella, introduced by Bernie Sanders
years.p: Senator Bernie Sanders and Rep. Maxwell Frost introduced her set, per Wikipedia, citing her advocacy on women's rights and Gaza.
years.xp: Clairo has also signed open letters on LGBT+ conversion therapy (July 2020) and Gaza (October 2023), and played Artists for Aid benefit concerts in London in January and July 2024, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Ayo Edebiri directs "Terrapin", with "Weird Al" Yankovic
years.p: The video for the Charm single arrived on February 6, 2025.

years.h: Clairo signs with Atlantic Records
years.p: Wikipedia lists the move as September 2025; Charm itself came out on her own Clairo Records imprint.
